title: The Derivative Payoff Bias (3rd Friday Price Spike)
one_line: Since 2003, S&P 500 prices drift up from Thursday's close into the 3rd-Friday morning settlement (SOQ, +18.2 bps, t = 4.5) and revert by midday; a long-Thursday-close / short-at-SOQ trade earned ~24 bps per expiry after costs.

findings.statement: On monthly expiration (3rd Friday), the opening settlement price (SOQ) is on average 18.2 bps above Thursday's close since 2003; no effect before 2003.
E-mini futures rise overnight, peak around the SOQ calculation, and revert; the reversal completes by midday.
findings.evidence: Overnight futures gain ~14 bps (t ≈ 3.5); SPX open-to-close on 3rd Fridays averages -16.4 bps.

findings.statement: A buy-Thursday-close, short-at-SOQ, close-at-Friday-close strategy grew $1 to ~$2.18 by 2021, Sharpe often above 2; mean 27 bps → 24 bps after costs (t ≈ 3.5).
findings.evidence: Backtest on the index via the SOQ (2003-2021), not on ES directly.

findings.statement: Appears in DJIA and Nasdaq-100 too; absent for p.m.-settled expiries.
Call payoffs inflated ~$214m/month, puts deflated ~$80m/month (~$3.5bn/yr lower bound).

why.pattern: Execution mechanics: option dealers' 'charm' hedging (delta decaying into expiry) forces predictable buying into the settlement.
why.mechanism: As expiry nears, dealers' hedges must be adjusted; the net adjustment is buying into the SOQ, which then reverts once settlement is fixed.
why.who_is_forced: Option dealers hedging expiring a.m.-settled SPX options.
why.why_it_persists: Tied to the expiry calendar and settlement design; published 2023-2024, so crowding is possible.
why.what_would_kill_it: Changes to SOQ settlement, shift of open interest to p.m.-settled / 0DTE contracts, or arbitrageurs front-running the overnight leg.
why.authors_explanation_vs_ours: Authors favour charm hedging and leave manipulation untested.

reported_results.headline: +18.2 bps Thursday close → SOQ (t = 4.5); ~24 bps per expiry after costs.
reported_results.costs_included: Yes, in the index backtest (27 → 24 bps).

tradable_edge: Monthly ES trade: buy at the Thursday 16:00 ET close before the 3rd-Friday expiry, sell at the Friday 09:30 open (the SOQ); optional second leg short from 09:30 to the close/midday. ~12 trades a year.
angles: Long leg only vs long + short legs

decay_risk.reason: Published 2023-2024 with press coverage ('manipulation talk'); small capacity; settlement-structure dependent.

data_fit: ES 1-min (ETH + RTH) Dec 2013 → Sep 2026 in clean_ES_master.parquet; NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026. 2024+ is protected in the backtest project. The overnight ETH bars capture the Thursday-close → Friday-open leg.
caveats: Small sample: ~12 trades a year → ~120 in ES 2014-2023.
The paper backtests the index SOQ, not ES fills; ES 09:30 open is a proxy for the SOQ.
